items.title: A spatiotemporal atlas of radiation-induced brain injury reveals dysfunction of the blood-CSF barrier.
items.authors: Cheng Quan; Yan Gao; Xinyi Liu; Jiabao Xiang; Jiashu Zhang; Liping Chen; Ying Li; Weiming Gao
items.abstract: Radiotherapy for brain tumors frequently induces irreversible cognitive decline, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we present an integrated single-cell and spatial transcriptomic atlas of radiation-induced brain injury (RIBI) in mice, spanning the acute to chronic phases. We reveal that the early-delayed phase following irradiation represents a critical window during which the blood-cerebrospinal fluid barrier (BCSFB) integrity is compromised. This disruption results from the selective depletion of a radiosensitive Tmsb4x+ epithelial subpopulation in the choroid plexus, which functions as a gatekeeper for the BCSFB. Consequently, CSF-derived macrophages excessively infiltrate the periventricular niche and engage in spatial crosstalk with interferon-responsive microglia. This dysregulated immune axis sustains chronic neuroinflammation, driving the late-stage neurodegeneration and cognitive impairment. In conclusion, our study establishes a high-resolution spatiotemporal framework and positions the BCSFB as a pivotal immune gateway and a promising therapeutic target for mitigating RIBI.

items.title: Chaihu-Jia-Longgu-Muli Tang ameliorates chronic restraint stress-induced depressive-like behaviors in association with modulation of the gut microbiota-NLRP3 inflammasome-microglia axis.
items.authors: Baoying Wang; Xinyu Yang; Zhe Xie; Zibo Li; Xiangli Yan; Yucheng Li; Ming Bai; Erping Xu
items.abstract: Chronic stress-induced neuroinflammation and gut microbiota dysbiosis have been implicated in the pathogenesis of depression. The classic herbal formula Chaihu-Jia-Longgu-Muli Tang (CLM) has been reported to exert antidepressant effects, but the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study aimed to investigate whether CLM ameliorates depressive-like behavior in chronic restraint stress (CRS)-induced mice and to explore its association with the gut microbiota remodeling, NLRP3 inflammasome signaling, and microglia activation. A mouse model of depression was established through exposure to CRS. Depressive-like behaviors were assessed using the sucrose preference test (SPT), tail suspension test (TST), and open field test (OFT). Hippocampal neuronal damage was evaluated by HE and Nissl staining. Intestinal barrier integrity was examined by HE staining and immunofluorescence staining for ZO-1 and occludin. Colonic and hippocampal levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines were measured by ELISA. Gut microbiota composition was analyzed by 16 S rRNA gene sequencing. Hippocampal M1 microglial polarization and microglial NLRP3 localization were assessed by Iba-1/CD86 and Iba-1/NLRP3 double immunofluorescence staining, and NLRP3 inflammasome-related protein expression was further evaluated by Western blotting. CLM attenuated CRS-induced depressive-like behaviors and hippocampal neuronal damage, restored gut barrier integrity as indicated by increased ZO-1 and occludin expression and reduced colonic IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-1β levels, and reshaped the gut microbiota by increasing SCFA-producing Muribaculaceae, Alloprevotella, and Bacteroides and decreasing Dubosiella and Lactobacillus spp. Exploratory Spearman analyses identified several nominal associations between microbial taxa and behavioral or inflammatory variables; however, these associations did not remain significant after Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction and should therefore be interpreted as hypothesis-generating. CLM-H also reduced hippocampal CD86⁺/Iba-1⁺ cells, decreased NLRP3+/Iba-1+ co-localization, and reduced NLRP3, caspase-1 p20, and pro-IL-1β expression. CLM-H ameliorates CRS-induced depressive-like behavior and neuronal damage in association with modulation of the gut microbiota composition, NLRP3 inflammasome-related signaling, and microglial activation. These findings support the potential of CLM as a multi-target intervention for depression-related phenotypes, while further causal validation is still required.

items.title: Apolipoprotein E4 and immune dysfunction in Alzheimer's disease: mechanisms and therapeutic implications.
items.authors: Hao Shi; Yang Zhao; Wei Zhu; Yan-Jiang Wang; Xian-Le Bu
items.abstract: Emerging evidence suggests that apolipoprotein E4 (APOE4) functions as an organizer of brain-periphery immune crosstalk, coupling maladaptive microglial states with peripheral immune remodeling to establish a self-reinforcing neuroimmune loop that may accelerate the progression of Alzheimer's disease. In the central nervous system, APOE4 pushes microglia away from homeostatic surveillance toward metabolically stressed, inflammatory, and synaptotoxic phenotypes, thereby weakening pathological protein clearance and promoting neurodegeneration. In the periphery, APOE4 primes innate and adaptive immune cells toward a pro-inflammatory state, creating a reservoir that can communicate with the diseased brain and infiltrate it. In addition, APOE4 erodes the separation between central and peripheral immune compartments, enabling bidirectional immune crosstalk that amplifies neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration. In this review, we synthesize evidence for APOE4-driven central and peripheral immune dysregulation; discuss therapeutic opportunities for targeting the APOE4 immune axis; and highlight the need for human-derived, longitudinal, cross-tissue studies to identify causal, stage-specific, and targetable immune nodes for precision intervention.

items.title: Brain Stimulation as a Treatment for Apathy: A Scoping Review of Effects and Safety.
items.journal: The Journal of neuropsychiatry and clinical neurosciences
items.authors: Parneet Grewal; Michael B Seidman; Joseph Chasen; Daniel Lench; Ivy Dickens; Emily A Brennan; Federico Rodriguez-Porcel; John Kindred
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Apathy is a neuropsychiatric syndrome characterized by impairment of goal-directed behavior, cognition, and emotional responsiveness. In this scoping review, the authors evaluated the literature on brain stimulation for the treatment of patients with apathy across diagnostic categories and provide recommendations to guide future research and practice. METHODS: The authors searched PubMed, Scopus, and PsycInfo for studies involving brain stimulation for apathy as a primary or secondary outcome. RESULTS: From 1,209 records, 52 studies evaluating brain stimulation were included; of these, 10 systematic reviews or meta-analyses were synthesized separately. Modalities included repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS; N=26), deep brain stimulation (DBS; N=7), transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS; N=6), electroconvulsive therapy (N=1), transcranial alternating current stimulation (N=1), and transcranial pulsating electromagnetic field therapy (N=1). Populations included patients with schizophrenia (N=477), Parkinson's disease (PD; N=289), depression (N=288), Alzheimer's disease (AD) and mild cognitive impairment (MCI) (N=210), Huntington's disease (N=42), PD with MCI (N=28), traumatic brain injury (N=28), stroke (N=14), COVID-19 (N=12), and dementia with Lewy bodies (N=6) (total N=1,366). rTMS improved apathy measures, most consistently in AD, with positive trends in depression, MCI, stroke, and schizophrenia. tDCS showed variable effects, with some benefits for schizophrenia. DBS showed mixed results, varying with stimulation location. Observed adverse events were mild and modality specific. CONCLUSIONS: Investigations into brain stimulation as a treatment for apathy show some promise. Conclusions were limited by small sample sizes, heterogeneous study designs, and variable outcome measures. Randomized trials with common validated apathy instruments, standardized stimulation parameters, and harmonized diagnostic measures may help advance the field.

items.title: Single-cell and spatial multi-omics reveal a recurrent multicellular niche at the tumor-stroma interface in multidrug resistance.
items.authors: Kangjie Shen; Lu Wang; Zixu Gao; Junquan Song; Qiangcheng Wang; Minying Deng; Yingcheng Wu; Yang Yang
items.abstract: Multi-drug resistance (MDR) is an almost inevitable endpoint of cancer therapy, driving rapid tumor progression, yet its evolutionary logic remains unclear because MDR tumors are rarely resected. Using paired therapy-naive and MDR melanoma specimens from a clinical trial, integrated with single-cell and spatial multi-omics and evaluated together with datasets from 10 additional cancer types, we identify a recurrent MDR-associated spatial nexus along the tumor-stroma interface. This niche juxtaposes CXCL14+ inflammatory cancer-associated fibroblasts (iCAFs), TREM2+ tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), and AXL+ dedifferentiated tumor cells, and is accompanied by loss of tumor-reactive CXCL13+CD8+ T cells. In vitro, CXCL14 promotes macrophage migration and TREM2 induction, while TREM2+ TAMs suppress CXCL13+CD8+ T cells via CD86-CTLA4 signaling. TREM2+ TAMs also promote tumor dedifferentiation through oleic acid-driven GAS6-AXL activation. We develop an FAP/TREM2-targeting bispecific antibody to disrupt this spatial nexus and restore therapeutic sensitivity in MDR patient-derived xenograft models with favorable safety.

items.title: Inhalation of Environmentally Simulated PET Nanoplastics Induces Demyelinating Disorders via the CXCL12/CXCR4 Axis.
items.authors: Shuang Liu; Jingcun Dong; Yu Hu; Qingqing Zhu; Huiyang Fu; Jia Gao; Xueyu Weng; Ligang Hu
items.abstract: The health threat from airborne nanoplastics (NPs) remains unclear, as despite inhalation being a more direct brain entry route than ingestion, current understanding relies on oral exposure and commercial particle models that obscure realistic risks. Here, by integrating environmentally simulated polyethylene terephthalate (PET)-NPs with an aerosol inhalation model that mirrors real-world human exposure (0.1, 1, and 10 mg/m3), we demonstrate that chronic NP inhalation translocated to the brain and induced demyelination, neuroinflammation, and cognitive deficits. The most pronounced effects were observed at the highest exposure dose (10 mg/m3), which is relevant to the occupational settings. Mechanistically, NP exposure triggered astrocytic CXCL12 release, leading to CXCR4-dependent microglial activation and cytokine network dysregulation. In vitro, blockade of CXCR4 with AMD3100 attenuated NP-induced microglial migration and oligodendrocytic myelin basic protein reduction. Our study thus definitively links realistic airborne NP exposure to the key neuropathological features of demyelinating disorders and pinpoints a modifiable molecular pathway that could inform exposure-based preventive strategies. These findings underscore the need for further assessment of airborne NP risks, particularly in occupational settings.

items.title: α-Catenin phosphorylation is tension-sensitive and supports epithelial barrier functions via afadin.
items.authors: Jeanne M Quinn; Phuong M Le; Anthea Weng; Annette S Flozak; S Sai Folmsbee; Erik Arroyo Colon; Raul Piseaux Aillon; Sonali I Jain
items.abstract: Zonula adherens junctions (zAJs) are spatially proximal to tight junctions (TJs), in a superstructure known as the apical junctional complex (AJC). A key component of the AJC is a circumferential ring of F-actin, but how actomyosin contractility drives AJC structure and epithelial barrier function is incompletely understood. Here, we show that a central mechanosensitive component of zAJ, α-catenin (α-cat), undergoes force-dependent phosphorylation in an unstructured linker region. This modification in turn primes the α-cat middle region for effector binding. We credential afadin, a TJ/AJ scaffold protein, as a mechanochemical binding partner of α-cat, identifying residues in α-cat required for binding. α-Cat phosphorylation and afadin binding support their co-enrichment at zAJ and barrier function. A mouse model that prevents α-cat phosphorylation is particularly detrimental to postnatal brain development, leading to hydrocephalus with junctional features similar to an afadin-binding mutant form of α-cat. These data support a model where α-cat integrates mechanical and chemical signals to progressively promote zAJ enrichment, effector recruitment, and barrier function.

items.title: Microtubules and nuclear pores position centromeres and genes in neural stem cells.
items.abstract: Chromatin's spatial organization is important for cell division, epigenetic memory, and gene regulation. Chromatin architecture is often reflected in nonrandom centromere positioning, which changes during development and disease. However, the mechanisms and functions of centromere positioning remain largely unknown. Here, we report that Drosophila neural stem cells cluster centromeres near the nuclear envelope, adjacent to the apical centrosome. This asymmetric centromere positioning persists throughout interphase but is lost in differentiated progeny. Asymmetric centromere positioning is regulated by microtubules from the apical centrosome connected to nuclear pore complexes (NPCs), generating a pulling force mediated by the motor protein Dynein and its binding partner Mushroom body defect. Lamin facilitates centromere-NPC binding, necessary for centromere positioning and clustering. We also find that the developmentally regulated genes hunchback and pendulin occupy specific nuclear regions, correlating with polarized centromere localization. We propose that fly neural stem cells translate their inherent polarity into stereotypical chromatin organization, potentially influencing cell-fate decisions and stem cell behavior.

items.title: Mechanisms of ubiquitination in central nervous system injury and potential therapeutic targets.
items.authors: Yun Shu; Yuheng Zhang; Yuzhe Wu; Linyi Xiang; Ruize Miao; Jiayi Zhao; Zhichao Tao; Jian Wang
items.abstract: Ubiquitination is a highly conserved and reversible post-translational modification that regulates protein stability, localization, activity, and intracellular signaling through the coordinated actions of the ubiquitin-proteasome system. In recent years, increasing evidence has highlighted the critical role of ubiquitination in maintaining central nervous system proteostasis and regulating pathological responses following central nervous system injury. This review comprehensively summarizes recent advances in research on ubiquitination in traumatic brain injury, spinal cord injury, stroke, and central nervous system infections, with particular emphasis on its involvement in secondary injury and subsequent neural repair. The mechanisms by which ubiquitination and deubiquitination regulate neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, blood-brain barrier integrity, and programmed cell death, including apoptosis, pyroptosis, necroptosis, and ferroptosis, are highlighted. Disease-specific ubiquitination patterns and their contributions to vascular repair, neural stem cell activation, axonal regeneration, and functional recovery are also discussed. Furthermore, emerging therapeutic strategies targeting key ubiquitin-system enzymes, as well as nanotechnology- and artificial intelligence-enabled approaches for precise modulation of ubiquitin-dependent signaling, are summarized and their therapeutic potential is explored. Although promising findings have been obtained from cellular and animal models, the cell-type-, temporal-, and disease-context-specific nature of ubiquitin signaling, substrate selectivity, and distinct ubiquitin-chain topologies remain major barriers to clinical translation. Further studies are therefore needed to elucidate the spatiotemporal dynamics of ubiquitination and identify context-specific therapeutic windows. Overall, ubiquitination represents a central regulatory network connecting proteostasis, neuroinflammation, cell death, and neural repair, providing a promising therapeutic approach for improving neurological outcomes after central nervous system injury.

items.title: Computer-assisted voice training for bilateral vocal fold paralysis following traumatic brain injury: a 26-month follow-up case report.
items.authors: Gang Fang; Qin Zhou; Chaolan Wang; Ren Zhuang
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the long-term efficacy of computer-assisted voice training in a patient with bilateral vocal fold paralysis (BVFP) following traumatic brain injury (TBI), a condition for which no standardized non-surgical protocol exists and long-term objective outcome data are entirely absent. METHODS: A 27-year-old female with severe TBI who developed BVFP after tracheostomy decannulation underwent 3 months of computer-assisted voice training (five sessions per week, 20 min per session) targeting maximum phonation time and vocal intensity via visual biofeedback. Voice outcomes were assessed using the Dysphonia Severity Index (DSI), maximum phonation time (MPT), jitter, shimmer, and the Voice Handicap Index-10 (VHI-10), with follow-ups at 6 and 26 months. Fiberoptic endoscopic evaluation of swallowing (FEES) was also performed. RESULTS: DSI improved dramatically from -22.28 at baseline to +0.73 at 26 months (a 23.01-point gain). MPT increased by 191% (from 8.60 s to 25.02 s, exceeding normative values), jitter normalized to 0.43%, and VHI-10 improved by 64.7% (from 34 to 12). FEES demonstrated improved vocal fold adduction with Penetration-Aspiration Scale improvement from 6 to 1. CONCLUSION: This case demonstrates that computer-assisted voice training can produce significant and sustained improvements in post-TBI BVFP, offering a viable non-surgical rehabilitation option for this rare complication. The 26-month follow-up provides the longest objective outcome data reported for this population.

top_journal_neuroscience.title: Preclinical and first-in-human evaluation of VG-3927/SAR448851, an oral small-molecule TREM2 agonist for Alzheimer's disease.
top_journal_neuroscience.authors: Borislav Dejanovic; Matthew D Figley; Elizabeth Weisman; Beril Kiragasi; Frederick W Gergits; Kelley Larson; Abigail Renoux; Raj Rajagovindan
top_journal_neuroscience.abstract: Microglial dysfunction is increasingly implicated in Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathogenesis, with loss-of-function variants in the microglial receptor TREM2 as major risk factors for late-onset AD. We report VG-3927, an oral, CNS-penetrant small-molecule TREM2 agonist that engages the transmembrane domains of TREM2 and its adaptor DAP12 to promote higher-order receptor complex formation and downstream signaling. VG-3927 and tool compound VG-3909 exhibited (sub)nanomolar potency, cooperated with endogenous ligands including amyloid-β (Aβ), and restored signaling in disease-associated TREM2 variants. In human iPSC-derived neuron-microglia-astrocyte cultures, VG-3927 reduced inflammatory cytokines and markers of neuronal damage. In 5xFAD amyloidosis mice expressing the common variant of hTREM2 (5xFAD;hTREM2CV), VG-3909 induced neuroprotective transcriptional reprogramming of microglia, particularly in the plaque niche; enhanced Aβ phagocytosis; and boosted brain glucose metabolism. By contrast, a TREM2 agonist antibody, which may be sequestered by soluble TREM2 (sTREM2), failed to engage plaque microglia. In a first-in-human, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 1 trial (NCT06343636, n = 115), VG-3927 was well tolerated across single and multiple ascending doses of up to 140 milligrams. Pharmacokinetics supported once-daily dosing with high CNS penetration (CSF-to-unbound plasma ratio of 0.91). VG-3927 induced dose-dependent reductions in CSF sTREM2, a biomarker of target engagement, consistent across healthy and elderly participants and participants with AD, supporting further clinical development in AD under the new designation SAR448851.

top_journal_neuroscience.title: An aging-sensitive secreted phospholipase confers neuroprotection and cognitive resilience.
top_journal_neuroscience.authors: Cinzia Vicidomini; Travis D Goode; Ruilin Yu; Iyanah Mehta; Kathleen M McAvoy; Connor H Beveridge; Caitlin E Randolph; Sanjay N Iyer
top_journal_neuroscience.abstract: Cognitive reserve theory posits that compensatory mechanisms during aging stave off cognitive decline and lower risk for Alzheimer's disease. Here, in a screen for hippocampal dentate granule cell (DGC) synapse loss-induced factors in mice, we identified a secreted phospholipase, Pla2g2f, whose expression increases in DGCs during aging and is associated with cognitive resilience in humans. Pla2g2f deletion in DGCs exacerbates aging-associated pathophysiological changes, including synapse loss, inflammatory microglia, reactive astrogliosis, impaired neurogenesis, lipid dysregulation, lipid droplet accumulation and hippocampal-dependent memory loss. Conversely, boosting Pla2g2f in DGCs during aging is sufficient to prevent these pathophysiological alterations in hippocampal-cortical circuits, protect memory and prophylactically modify trajectory of cognitive decline. Mutagenesis of the catalytic site of PLA2G2F prevented lipid droplet mobilization and reduction of reactive gliosis and inflammatory microglia. Neuronal PLA2G2F mediates intercellular signaling to decrease lipid droplet and cholesterol ester load in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived microglia. Our findings implicate PLA2G2F as a compensatory neuroprotective broadcast signal that maintains lipid homeostasis to counteract aging-associated cognitive decline.

top_journal_neuroscience.title: EGFR-targeted antibody-toxin conjugate in recurrent glioma: a phase 1 trial.
top_journal_neuroscience.authors: Vidyalakshmi Chandramohan; James E Herndon; Anjali Barnwal; Katayoun Ayasoufi; Weixuan Yan; Kevin Stevenson; Michelle L Bowie; Michael C Brown
top_journal_neuroscience.abstract: D2C7-ATC is a recombinant antibody-toxin conjugate (ATC) targeting wild-type epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and mutant EGFR variant III (EGFRvIII). We conducted a single-arm, single-site, open-label phase 1 trial evaluating a single infusion of D2C7-ATC via convection-enhanced delivery in the enhancing disease of 81 patients with biopsy-confirmed recurrent malignant glioma. The primary objective was to determine toxicity and the recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D) of D2C7-ATC. Secondary objectives included describing overall survival (OS) and assessing the association between EGFR expression and OS. The median overall survival (mOS) was 7.9 months among 72 patients with isocitrate dehydrogenase wild-type recurrent glioblastoma (IDHwt rGBM), including 35 patients in the dose-escalation stage (40 to 35,032 ng ml-1) and 37 patients in the dose-expansion stage (RP2D of 6,920 ng ml-1). D2C7-ATC was generally well tolerated, with mainly grade 1-2 treatment-related adverse events (67%). The maximum tolerated dose was exceeded at 35,032 ng ml-1, where four patients experienced dose-limiting toxicities, including grade 4 (N = 2) and grade 3 (N = 2) events. Eight patients died on trial; all deaths were unrelated to D2C7-ATC. Univariate analyses identified survival-associated biomarkers, including tumor D2C7 antibody reactivity, circulating cytokines, a tumor inflammatory gene signature and neutrophils, monocytes and lymphocytes in blood. Notably, patients with IDHwt rGBM with a D2C7 antibody reactivity score of <1.5+ in pre-treatment tumor had an mOS of 17.38 months, whereas those with low IL-8 in post-treatment plasma had an mOS of 16.6 months. These findings indicate that EGFR-targeted D2C7-ATC therapy prolongs survival in a subset of patients with IDHwt rGBM via intratumoral and systemic immune activation. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT02303678 .

top_journal_neuroscience.title: Elp1 is required for myeloid differentiation and brain repopulation.
top_journal_neuroscience.authors: Marius Marc-Daniel Mader; Wanhua Li; Alexa Scavetti; Yongjin Yoo; Gernot Neumayer; Katie Han; Yohei Shibuya; Michael Haney
top_journal_neuroscience.abstract: Haematopoietic stem and progenitor cell (HSPC) transplantation-mediated replacement of microglia-the reconstitution of the central nervous system microglial niche with donor-derived myeloid cells-represents a promising strategy for brain cell therapies1-7. However, the cell-intrinsic molecular regulators of HSPC-derived myeloid lineage commitment in the brain have remained largely uncharacterized. This is partially because the scarcity of primary HSPCs has rendered large-scale genetic interrogation intractable. Here we explored whether ex vivo expansion of primary cultured HSPCs (cHSPCs) enables unbiased genetic interrogation of haematopoietic differentiation. We established that cHSPCs can be genetically manipulated and readily differentiate into myeloid cells and repopulate microglia niches of the brain after transplantation. Moreover, primary neonatal astrocytes contained strong signals to induce myeloid specification of cHSPCs in vitro. To identify genes that regulate glia-induced myeloid differentiation, we successfully screened around 20,000 individual genetic perturbations and characterized genes involved in the regulation of cell signalling, cell cycle, mitochondrial function and protein translation. Among these genes was elongator acetyltransferase complex subunit 1 (Elp1), which suppressed the unfolded protein response during myeloid specification and was essential for the generation but not maintenance of myeloid cells. Our work establishes a platform to investigate the molecular mechanisms of brain myeloid biology.

top_journal_neuroscience.title: Extracellular vesicle α-synuclein topology reveals disease-associated conformers in brain and blood.
top_journal_neuroscience.authors: Suman Dutta; Amin Atashgaran; Anis Sahoo; Stelios Chatzimichail; Achillefs N Kapanidis; George K Tofaris
top_journal_neuroscience.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD), dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), and multiple system atrophy (MSA) are unified by pathological α-synuclein (αSyn) aggregation, yet diverge in terms of the cellular distribution of pathology and clinical phenotype. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) have emerged as potential mediators or biomarkers of αSyn pathology, but whether their molecular constituents in the brain reflect disease-specific processes or conformations remains unknown. Here, we combined EV isolation, electrochemiluminescence, quantitative mass spectrometry and nanoscale single-vesicle imaging by direct stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy (dSTORM) to map the topology, epitope exposure and cellular origin of αSyn in EVs isolated from post-mortem PD, DLB, MSA, and healthy control (HC) brains and assessed the tractability of these molecular signatures in blood. Proteomics and immunoblotting of EV lysates isolated from human brains confirmed that they were highly purified and derived from neurons and glial cell subtypes. Across diseases, αSyn association with EVs exhibited distinct patterns: In PD and DLB, both total αSyn levels normalised to CD81 and the percentage of neuronal (L1CAM+) EVs with aggregated αSyn as detected by aggregate-preferring antibodies, were increased, whereas in MSA, aggregated αSyn was detected primarily in neuronal and to a lesser extent glial EV subpopulations without an increase in total EV-associated αSyn. Further epitope mapping by dSTORM identified a distinct αSyn conformational arrangement, as detected by antibodies against an epitope spanning αSyn residues 34-45, that was enriched on the surface of L1CAM+ EVs in MSA compared to PD. This N-terminal immunoreactive conformer was tractable in serum and enriched on the surface of L1CAM+ EVs from MSA compared to PD patients or controls. Collectively, our findings suggest that the epitope accessibility and topology of EV-associated αSyn proteoforms, rather than their abundance alone, discriminate synucleinopathy subtypes, offering a framework for a blood-based conformational stratification of these disorders.

top_journal_neuroscience.title: CHCHD2 mitigates age-associated proteostatic collapse by maintaining homeostasis of the mitochondria-lysosome axis.
top_journal_neuroscience.authors: Teresa R Kee; Brianna M Masters; Khoi D Tran; Hanna Jeon; Ma Long; Grace Xu; Sophia A Khan; Edwin Vázquez-Rosa
top_journal_neuroscience.abstract: Mutations in coiled-coil-helix-coiled-coil-helix domain containing 2 (CHCHD2), including the Parkinson's disease (PD)-linked CHCHD2T61I mutation, are associated with Lewy body disorders (LBDs) by unknown mechanisms. Here, we demonstrate that CHCHD2T61I exacerbates age-related brain pathologies, including axonal degeneration and cognitive deficits, by disrupting the mitochondria-lysosome axis. Specifically, CHCHD2T61I binds and reduces cathepsin B (CTSB) and cathepsin L (CTSL) levels, inducing lysosomal membrane permeability and impairing α-synuclein fibril clearance. We also demonstrate that human CHCHD2 declines in the brain with age, while expression of wild-type CHCHD2 safeguards against age-related neuroinflammation, dopaminergic neuron loss, insoluble protein aggregation, and structural deterioration of mitochondria and lysosomes. These findings, supported by observed reductions in CTSB and CHCHD2 in human LBD brains, establish CHCHD2 as a key regulator of neuronal resilience to aging and proteostatic collapse via the mitochondria-lysosome axis. Preventing age-associated CHCHD2 decline offers a therapeutic strategy to preserve brain health throughout aging.

top_journal_neuroscience.title: Molecular predictors of minimal residual disease in newly diagnosed multiple myeloma treated with quadruplet therapy.
top_journal_neuroscience.authors: Florence Magrangeas; Mia Cherkaoui; Victor Bessonneau-Gaborit; Jennifer Derrien; Céline Chevalier; Catherine Guérin-Charbonnel; Benjamin Diamond; Mehmet Kemal Samur
top_journal_neuroscience.abstract: Quadruplet therapy, combining anti-CD38 antibodies, immunomodulatory drugs, proteasome inhibitors and dexamethasone, is now the standard induction treatment for newly diagnosed multiple myeloma (NDMM). However, treatment response is heterogeneous and molecular predictors are needed to guide early therapeutic decisions. We performed integrated genomic, transcriptomic and epigenomic profiling of 423 tumor samples from patients with NDMM from the MIDAS cohort to characterize molecular heterogeneity and its association with measurable residual disease (MRD) after quadruplet induction with isatuximab, carfilzomib, lenalidomide and dexamethasone (Isa-KRd). Postinduction MRD-negativity rates varied significantly across gene expression subtypes, with HP1/HP3 and MS groups showing superior responses compared to the MF and CD2 subtypes. B cell differentiation was associated with MRD positivity, while proliferation and MYC programs were associated with MRD negativity. These MRD-associated transcriptomic features were independently validated in the CASSIOPEIA cohort. Whole-genome sequencing revealed both known (APOBEC mutagenesis, chromothripsis) and new genomic instability phenotypes validated in the MMRF cohort. New driver alterations were identified with independent validation across three external cohorts with multiple myeloma (MMRF, MANHATTAN and CASSIOPEIA; 1,451 cases). Genomic instability features and driver genes such as CCND1 and MYC correlated with differential MRD outcomes. DNA methylation profiling identified nine MRD-linked subgroups distinguished by the extent of hypomethylation in quiescent chromatin and cis/trans signatures of driver translocations. A multimodal random forest model integrating genomic, transcriptomic and epigenomic features predicted MRD status after induction, with an area under the curve of 0.77, outperforming clinical and genomic models, while providing comparable discrimination and improved calibration relative to the transcriptomic and epigenomic models. These findings define a multiomic classification of NDMM linked to Isa-KRd response. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT04934475 .

top_journal_neuroscience.title: Vascular Risk Factors and Late-Onset Epilepsy.
top_journal_neuroscience.authors: Hyunmi Choi; Jose Gutierrez; Tian Wang; Minghua Liu; Cheng-Shiun Leu; Sylwia Misiewicz; Jiying Han; Natalie A Bello
top_journal_neuroscience.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Late-onset epilepsy (LOE; onset at age ≥65 years) is increasingly recognized in older adults and may be associated with vascular risk. OBJECTIVE: To identify vascular risk factors (VRFs) associated with incident LOE in older adults. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This study is an individual participant data meta-analysis of 6 US population-based prospective cohort studies (the Epilepsy-Cog Study). In 5 cohorts linked to Medicare for epilepsy case ascertainment, follow-up for LOE began when a participant had accrued 2 years of continuous fee-for-service enrollment and was 65 years of age or older and extended to the end of continuous enrollment. Claims linkage covered 1991-2018 in the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Study (ARIC), 1992-2019 in the Cardiovascular Health Study (CHS), 2000-2019 in the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA), 2000-2020 in the Reasons for Geographic and Racial Differences in Stroke Study (REGARDS), and 1999-2019 in the Washington Heights/Inwood Columbia Aging Project (WHICAP). In the Northern Manhattan Study (NOMAS), which was not Medicare linked and used cohort-based epilepsy case ascertainment, follow-up for LOE began at cohort entry in 1993-2008 and extended to 2024. Data analysis was completed in January 2026. EXPOSURES: Sociodemographic characteristics and VRFs assessed by self-report, examinations, laboratory measures, and medication use. MAIN OUTCOME AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was incident LOE. Associations between risk factors and incident LOE were evaluated using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models to estimate hazard ratios. RESULTS: From 43 753 participants in Epilepsy-Cog, 551 participants with prevalent epilepsy and 945 with no follow-up after Epilepsy-Cog baseline were excluded. Among 42 257 participants (mean [SD] age, 71.4 [6.9] years; 23 383 [56.0%] female) followed up for a mean (SD) of 9.3 (6.2) years, 1500 participants (3.5%) developed LOE (3.8 per 1000 person-years). In fully adjusted models, LOE risk was higher with current smoking (HR = 1.39; 95% CI, 1.18-1.64), hypertension (HR = 1.17; 95% CI, 1.04-1.31), diabetes (HR = 1.42; 95% CI, 1.25-1.62), chronic kidney disease (HR = 1.29; 95% CI, 1.13-1.48), history of stroke (HR = 1.99; 95% CI, 1.63-2.43), and apolipoprotein E ε4 allele (1 ε4 allele: HR = 1.22; 95% CI, 1.07-1.39; 2 ε4 alleles: HR = 1.84; 95% CI, 1.36-2.50). Associations of VRFs with LOE were similar across age, sex, and race and ethnicity subgroups. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this pooled analysis of 6 US cohorts, multiple VRFs and a history of stroke were associated with incident LOE. These findings suggest that LOE may reflect the underlying burden of brain vascular disease.

global_hot_topics.title: Predicting IGD treatment outcomes across interventions using a whole-brain functional connectome biomarker.
global_hot_topics.authors: Meiting Wei; Xin Luo; Jiejie Fu; Shuang Li; Haosen Ni; Jiang Liu; Guang-Heng Dong
global_hot_topics.abstract: BACKGROUND: Although treatment approaches have been explored in internet gaming disorder (IGD), however, little is known about the specific neural activity that is associated with treatment outcomes. This study aims to establish a treatment-sensitive network that reliably predicts treatment outcomes across different interventions for IGD. METHODS: Resting-state fMRI data were collected from 90 individuals with IGD who received one of three different intervention protocols (mindfulness meditation, approach bias modification, or retrieval-aversive conditioning training). Connectome-based predictive modelling (CPM) was used to build a treatment-sensitive network to predict individual symptom reduction, then validated them on the external dataset. RESULTS: The negative (r = 0.401, p <.001) and combined network (r = 0.480, p <.001) can significantly predict a reduction of addiction severity (baseline minus post-test). Specifically, the negative network was primarily centred on the motor, subcortical, and salience networks. The positive network primarily involved cerebellar-related connections. Incorporating these into a combined model significantly improved predictive accuracy, suggesting that cerebellar-related connectivity may contribute to the prediction of intervention-related clinical improvement. Finally, the treatment-sensitive network was validated in a separate data. CONCLUSIONS: This study established a treatment-sensitive network based on the whole-brain connectome. These findings provide valuable empirical evidence for identifying biomarkers for IGD treatment and advance personalised therapeutic strategies. CLINICAL TRIALS REGISTRATION: The trial protocol was pre-registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (www.chictr.org.cn; ChiCTR2300077831(MM), ChiCTR2300075869(ApBm), ChiCTR2500095444(R-AC), ChiCTR2400090834(SAE)).

global_hot_topics.journal: PCN reports : psychiatry and clinical neurosciences
global_hot_topics.authors: Daud Gul; Sonia Khan; Kushal Baral; Ziad Saber; Arindam Ghosh; Eemaz Nathaniel; Onuwabhagbe Daniel Omomhenle; Nathaniel Oluwakayode Oyedeji
global_hot_topics.abstract: Centanafadine is a multimodal norepinephrine-dopamine-serotonin reuptake inhibitor (NDSRI) that has been evaluated for the treatment of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) across pediatric, adolescent, and adult populations. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of centanafadine compared with placebo, with particular emphasis on dose-response patterns across different age groups. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) were searched from database inception to July 2026. Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials evaluating centanafadine in patients with ADHD were eligible for inclusion. The Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool was used to assess the risk of bias. Because of differences in populations, formulations, dosing regimens, outcome measures, and reported effect estimates, findings were synthesized narratively rather than quantitatively. Four randomized trials reported in three publications, including 1845 randomized participants, were included. In children, high-dose centanafadine significantly improved attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder rating scale, version 5 (ADHD-RS-5) scores compared with placebo (-16.3 vs. -10.8; p < 0.001), whereas the low-dose group did not demonstrate a statistically significant difference (mean difference [MD] -2.7; 95% confidence interval [CI], -6.0 to 0.5; p = 0.10). In adolescents, 328.8 mg significantly improved ADHD-RS-5 scores compared with placebo (-18.5 vs. -14.2; p = 0.0006; Cohen's d = -0.40), whereas 164.4 mg did not (p = 0.3016). In adults, both 200 and 400 mg/day significantly improved Adult ADHD Investigator Symptom Rating Scale (AISRS) scores, with LSMDs ranging from -2.74 to -4.42 (p ≤ 0.039). Treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 25%-39% of children, 23.8%-50.3% of adolescents, and 17.6%-31.8% of adults, with higher rates generally observed at higher doses in some populations. Centanafadine demonstrated improvement in core ADHD symptoms across pediatric, adolescent, and adult populations, with a more apparent dose-response pattern in children and adolescents and significant efficacy across the adult doses evaluated. Higher doses were associated with increased treatment-emergent adverse events in some populations. However, the evidence base remains limited to four randomized trials from three publications, with predominantly short-term follow-up, no active-comparator trials, and limited independently sponsored evidence. Therefore, the efficacy, safety, and dose-response findings should be interpreted cautiously. Longer term, independently sponsored, and head-to-head comparative trials are needed to further establish the optimal dosing, comparative effectiveness, and long-term safety of centanafadine.

global_hot_topics.abstract: Suicidal ideation, depressive symptoms, anxiety, and sleep disturbance remain difficult to manage in psychiatric populations, and intermittent theta-burst stimulation (iTBS) has emerged as an accelerated, non-invasive neuromodulation strategy for these outcomes. This meta-analysis compares iTBS versus sham-iTBS across suicidal ideation, depression severity, anxiety severity, and sleep quality to guide clinical decision-making. We systematically searched relevant electronic databases in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. Continuous outcomes were pooled as standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals using random-effects inverse-variance models in RevMan 5.4. Heterogeneity was assessed using I 2 and χ 2 statistics, and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were performed. A p value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Six studies were included. iTBS significantly reduced suicidal ideation versus sham-iTBS (SMD = -0.51; 95% CI: -0.93 to -0.09; p = 0.02; I 2 = 70%; n = 181 vs. 157), and the effect remained significant with lower heterogeneity after exclusion of Qin et al. (p = 0.02; I 2 = 29%). Depression severity improved with iTBS (SMD = -1.06; 95% CI: -1.64 to -0.48; p = 0.0003; I 2 = 80%; n = 162 vs. 142), with heterogeneity decreasing to 24% after exclusion of Huang et al. Anxiety severity also improved (SMD = -0.68; 95% CI: -1.27 to -0.09; p = 0.02; I 2 = 79%; n = 139 vs. 120), and heterogeneity decreased to 38% after exclusion of Huang et al. Secondary analyses suggested improvements in depression and anxiety severity, whereas sleep quality did not differ between groups. Larger, standardized randomized controlled trials with longer follow-up are needed to determine the magnitude and durability of any antisuicidal effect.

global_hot_topics.title: TOMM5 is associated with oral cancer progression: a multi-omics analysis from single-cell atlas to in vitro validation.
global_hot_topics.authors: Li Gao; Jian-Di Li; Yi-Yang Chen; Ge-Li Tan; Jian-Jia Zeng; Xi Lin; Lu Liang; Shuang Xia
global_hot_topics.abstract: AIMS: Translocase of Outer Mitochondrial Membrane 5 (TOMM5), a mitochondrial outer membrane translocase subunit implicated in tumorigenesis, remains unexplored in oral cancer. Herein, we aimed to decipher the role of TOMM5 in oral cancer. METHODS: This study comprehensively explored the expression profile, clinical significance, and functional roles of TOMM5 in oral carcinogenesis with global RNA-seq and microarray datasets. In vitro experiments were performed for evaluating the impact of TOMM5 knockdown on the biological functions of oral cancer cells. Distribution heterogeneity of TOMM5 expression and related cellular trajectory was analyzed through scRNA-seq. The therapeutic implications of TOMM5 for oral cancer were analyzed through drug sensitivity prediction and tumor immune dysfunction and exclusion (TIDE) scoring. RESULTS: TOMM5 was significantly overexpressed in oral cancer tissues and demonstrated moderate diagnostic accuracy. TOMM5 knockdown significantly suppressed aggressive biological behaviors of oral cancer cells. ScRNA-seq data revealed predominant TOMM5 expression in B cells, decreasing with differentiation, and linked distinct pathway activities to specific cellular compartments. High TOMM5 expression was linked to reduced immune cell infiltration and sensitivity to Paclitaxel/Vincristine. CONCLUSIONS: Overexpressed TOMM5 shows potential as a biomarker in oral cancer, correlating with tumor progression and immune infiltration. Oral cancer remains a major health challenge with stagnant survival rates, highlighting the need for better biomarkers and therapeutic targets. We investigated TOMM5, a mitochondrial outer membrane protein, in oral cancer using transcriptomic data from over 300 tumors and normal tissues, along with functional experiments in cancer cells. Our results showed that TOMM5 is significantly overexpressed in oral cancer tissues and that high expression predicts poorer overall and disease‑free survival. Silencing TOMM5 in WSU‑HN30 oral cancer cells reduced their migratory and invasive abilities, without affecting proliferation. Single‑cell RNA sequencing revealed that TOMM5 is predominantly expressed in B cells within the tumor microenvironment and declines with cell differentiation. High TOMM5 expression correlated with reduced immune infiltration, particularly activated mast cells and neutrophils, and with increased myeloid‑derived suppressor cells, suggesting an immunosuppressive role. Furthermore, patients with elevated TOMM5 showed predicted sensitivity to paclitaxel and vincristine. In summary, TOMM5 overexpression is associated with tumor progression, immune modulation, and drug response in oral cancer, making it a promising biomarker and potential therapeutic guide. Additional experimental validation is warranted to confirm these findings.

global_hot_topics.title: Human-Derived Motor Neuron Progenitor Cell Implantation Rescues Motor Endplates Following Peripheral Nerve Injury.
global_hot_topics.journal: Journal of hand surgery global online
global_hot_topics.authors: Luigi P Gonzales; Chris Lee; Arjun T Gupta; David J Wright; Tyler R Johnston; Sang Ho Yoon; Robert Hunt; Oswald Steward
global_hot_topics.abstract: PURPOSE: Degradation of motor endplates (MEPs) following peripheral nerve injury (PNI) is a major determinant of functional recovery, as prolonged denervation renders target muscles progressively unreceptive to reinnervation. While prior studies have demonstrated that stem cell-based therapies may provide neurotrophic support following PNI, their potential effects on MEP preservation have not been well studied. We hypothesized that transplantation of human-induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived motor neuron progenitors (MNPs) into chronically denervated muscle would be associated with preservation of MEP architecture. METHODS: With Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee approval, chronic denervation injuries were created in mice via sciatic nerve transection. After 4 months of denervation, when MEPs have consistently degraded in this animal model, the denervated tibialis anterior (TA) was injected with low-dose MNPs (10,000 cells), high-dose MNPs (500,000 cells), or phosphate-buffered saline (negative control). Using a previously established method, hiPSCs were differentiated into functional MNPs prior to injection. At selected time points post-injection, the TA was harvested and immunostained to confirm MNP viability and detect the presence of MEPs. RESULTS: Transplanted MNPs remained viable within host muscle at both evaluated time points. No identifiable MEPs were detected in phosphate-buffered saline-treated chronically denervated muscle. In contrast, MNP-treated muscles demonstrated the presence of MEP-like structures following prolonged denervation. Qualitative differences in MEP density and morphologic complexity were observed between treatment groups, with greater preservation seen in the higher-dose cohort. Contralateral uninjured muscles demonstrated intact native MEP architecture. CONCLUSIONS: Intramuscular transplantation of hiPSC-derived MNPs into chronically denervated muscle was associated with preservation of MEP morphology in this preclinical proof-of-concept model. These preliminary findings suggest that cellular therapies may represent a potential adjunctive strategy to preserve end-organ receptivity following delayed peripheral nerve injury. TYPE OF STUDY/LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Preclinical controlled animal study, Level V.

global_hot_topics.authors: Arghavan Nepton; Sonya C Faber; Zachary Kaminsky; Mario Nucci; Hesam Farahani; Monnica T Williams; Sergio R Perez Rosal
global_hot_topics.abstract: Ketamine produces rapid antidepressant effects, but the molecular processes associated with their persistence remain poorly defined in humans. We examined longitudinal DNA methylation changes in 10 adults with major depressive disorder undergoing ketamine-assisted psychotherapy using two pre-treatment assessments (T1, T2) and one post-treatment assessment (T3). Participants received three sessions of intranasal racemic ketamine within a structured psychotherapy protocol. Buccal DNA methylation was measured using the Illumina MethylationEPIC v2.0 BeadChip. Depressive symptoms improved markedly following treatment, with mean Beck Depression Inventory-II scores declining from the severe to the mild range (p < .001). Of 802,595 CpG loci evaluated, 20,770 met the nominal T3-versus-T2 screening criterion. Sequential filtering for methylation-change magnitude and movement relative to pre-treatment fluctuation identified 962 retained CpG loci, including 517 retained gene-annotated loci. A supplementary linear mixed-effects analysis modeled repeated measurements within participants across the 603 preselected gene-annotated magnitude-filtered loci; because these loci were selected using the same contrast and cohort, this analysis was not treated as independent confirmation. Exploratory enrichment analysis of this 603-locus set identified NOTCH1-related Reactome terms driven by NOTCH1, DLL1, and ADAM17. Within the retained signature, multiple core and adjacent Notch-related components formed a coherent signaling module spanning ligand, receptor processing, transcriptional regulation, and pathway cross-talk. These findings identify a structured peripheral methylation signature associated with ketamine-assisted psychotherapy. They do not establish brain-specific pathway activation or causality, but provide a longitudinal basis for investigating regulatory adaptations accompanying clinical improvement.

global_hot_topics.title: Midlife and Late-Life Alzheimer Disease Blood Biomarkers and 11-Year Cognitive Decline.
global_hot_topics.authors: Jason R Smith; James Russell Pike; Yifei Lu; Keenan A Walker; Kevin J Sullivan; B Gwen Windham; Bharat Thyagarajan; Michelle M Mielke
global_hot_topics.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Plasma biomarkers of Alzheimer disease (AD) neuropathology (amyloid-β42 to amyloid β40 [Aβ42/40] ratio, phosphorylated tau at threonine [p-tau181]), neurodegeneration (neurofilament light [NfL]), and neuroinflammation (glial fibrillary acidic protein [GFAP]) in late-life are associated with cognitive decline. Whether these biomarkers in midlife are predictive of subsequent cognitive decline, and whether they are associated with different cognitive domains, is uncertain. In this study, we investigated associations of midlife and late-life plasma Aβ42/40, p-tau181, NfL, and GFAP with late-life change in domain-specific (memory, language, and executive function) and global cognitive function. METHODS: We performed a prospective cohort analysis of the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Neurocognitive Study (ARIC-NCS). Outcome follow-up was from ARIC visit 5 (2011-2013) to visit 9 (2021-2022). We included all individuals from ARIC field centers (Jackson, Mississippi; Forsyth County, North Carolina; Washington County, Maryland; and Minneapolis suburbs, Minnesota) with biomarkers measured from stored specimens in midlife (visit 3, 1993-1995, mean age 59.0 years) and late-life (visit 5, 2011-2013, mean age 76.8 years). Aβ42/40, p-tau181, NfL, and GFAP were measured with the Quanterix Simoa platform and standardized to visit 3 to facilitate cross-biomarker comparisons of their rate of change from midlife to late-life. We estimated change in memory, language, executive function, and global cognition factor scores from visit 5 to visit 9 with linear mixed-effect models. RESULTS: In 1,515 included participants, 60.7% (n = 920) were female and 25.5% (n = 387) were Black. Each SD increase in p-tau181 in midlife was significantly associated with faster late-life memory decline (β = -0.030 [95% CI -0.059 to -0.001] SD. Midlife Aβ42/40, NfL, and GFAP were not associated with subsequent decline in any cognitive domain. In late-life, p-tau181, NfL, and GFAP were significantly associated with faster decline in different cognitive domains, with the strongest associations seen with memory (β = -0.091 [95% CI -0.123 to -0.058] SD; β = -0.064 [95% CI -0.106 to -0.023] SD; and β = -0.048 [95% CI -0.082 to -0.013] SD, respectively). DISCUSSION: Midlife p-tau181 was associated with faster 11-year memory decline beginning 20 years later in the ARIC cohort, which underscores a potentially long prodromal phase of cognitive decline that could precede dementia onset. In late-life, biomarkers for AD, neurodegeneration, and neuroinflammation were associated with faster decline across different cognitive domains, but associations remained strongest for p-tau181 and memory.

global_hot_topics.title: Glioblastoma immune landscape remodeling following treatment with CD70-targeted CAR-T cells.
global_hot_topics.authors: Alexandros Kourtesakis; Dennis Alexander Agardy; Clara Tejido Dierssen; Ling Hai; Dirk Carsten Frieder Hoffmann; Normann Mussnig; Ralph Sinn; Manuel Fischer
global_hot_topics.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy has shown limited efficacy in glioblastoma (GB), largely because of the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). We have previously demonstrated that the ligand-based mCD70-directed construct mCAR27 specifically eliminates CD70⁺ GB cells in vitro, and induces durable tumor remission with prolonged survival in a syngeneic model of orthotopic GB. Despite the therapeutic promise of CD70 as a GB CAR-T cell target, the impact of CD70-directed CAR-T cells on the brain tumor immune landscape after target interception remains unexplored. Here, we independently confirmed a tumorigenic role for CD70 in murine GB by performing bulk RNA sequencing and in vivo experiments. Next, we applied single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNAseq) to decipher the transcriptome of GB-infiltrating immune cells in immunocompetent mice bearing CD70+ GB after intratumoral mCAR27 therapy. CAR-T cell treatment expanded adoptively transferred cells and was associated with increased endogenous Cd8⁺ T-cell infiltration, alongside a reduction in immunosuppressive populations, including Tregs and anti-inflammatory M2-like macrophages, but also subsets of dendritic and natural-killer cells. CD70 expression was detected on multiple GB-infiltrating immune subsets, notably Tregs and M2-like macrophages. Transcriptionally, mCAR27-mediated GB remission led to a coordinated downregulation of type-I interferon-stimulated genes and immunosuppressive mediators such as Arg1, Tgfbi, Cd274, Pdcd1lg2 and Lag3, coupled with upregulation of genes involved in inflammatory resolution, findings consistent with attenuation of GB-derived inflammatory stress and immunosuppression. Collectively, we showcase that CD70-directed CAR-T cell therapy remodels the post-treatment immune landscape towards resolution of inflammation and reduced immunosuppression, supporting sustained immune surveillance.
